metas.name: Açai Palms
metas.note: Açai palms produce fruits that are popular globally. Most of these palms are found near Belem, but can be seen across the Amazon. They are distinct in the way the leaflets droop downward along with their unusually thin trunks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Babassu Palms
metas.note: Babassu palms have long, robust leaves comprised of many leaflets. Trunk length can vary from short to tall. They are found throughout the Amazon, or more rarely, down the east coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Carnaúba Palms
metas.note: Carnaúba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in Ceará but are also in Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Coconut Palm Trees
metas.note:
Coconut palm trees have long leaves, can grow very tall, and have thin trunks. They are common across the north eastern states and sometimes further west or south along the coast.

NOTE: Coconut palms grow across the world and are not unique to Brazil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Coffee Bean Plantations
metas.note:
Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.

Use in combination with landscape and soil color to get a vibe for which region the coffee is from.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Eucalyptus Grandis
metas.note: Eucalyptus Grandis, when fully grown, is a very tall tree with plantations all over Brazil. You can find them in both large and very small plantations., as well as randomly growing anywhere. You can see them all over the south, but there are some large plantations in Amapá too.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Long Stem Plant on Roadside
metas.note: This species of plant, with long stems and many leaves growing up, are very common in Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, and Paraíba. In the dry season, you can still make out the distinct long stems without leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Macaw Palms
metas.note: Macaw palms have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Moriche Palms
metas.note:
Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape. They are most common in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima, but can be found in all of the Amazonian states.

NOTE: These palms can additionally be found very commonly in the Amazonian parts of Colombia and Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Paraná Pines
metas.note: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Soybeans
metas.note: Soybeans appear as small, leafy soil grown plants. They are most commonly grown in Mato Grosso, Paraná, and Goiás.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Sugarcane Plantations
metas.note:
Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of São Paulo, and in the coastal north east states, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

As a rule of thumb: The sugarcane plantations in the south will more often have red soil, while the ones in Alagoas and Pernambuco will be more yellow/white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Tocantins Grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.
